handled_verified._description: the analyzer emits correctly (probe/fixture-confirmed). A type belongs here only if it contributes a symbol or a relationship, OR the analyzer deliberately consults it to refuse an emission (ERROR — the scoped damage guard at real-javascript-analyzer.ts:302, the same ruling as bash BD5). A node the analyzer merely reads but attributes elsewhere (e.g. a class EXPRESSION, whose heritage rides its binding) is RULED under design_decision instead, not asserted here.

internal_silent._description: container/literal/keyword correctly emitting nothing. Also holds the tree-sitter synthetic error-recovery marker MISSING: not a grammar construct, emits no symbol — the same guard that covers ERROR reports it on result.errors.

gaps.node_type: overrides — compared for javascript with NO truth behind it, and ~a fifth of the edges it emits name members that cannot exist on the base
gaps.missing: TWO defects in one label. (1) `overrides` is in the javascript comparison set and the oracle derives no `overrides` truth at all, so every analyzer override edge is unmatched — the same shape as the `imports` and `extends` gaps, and the third instance in this lane. (2) The edges are largely unfounded: the analyzer matches method NAMES across a class boundary to a base it cannot resolve, and emits `overrides` for names that cannot be members of that base.
gaps.evidence: **HOW (1) WAS FOUND, which is the reusable part.** A gated per-label truth dump (BB_LABEL_DUMP) prints, per label, how many TRUTH rows the oracle derived and how many ANALYZER rows were comparable. A label with `truth=0` and `comparable>0` is being compared against nothing. That check found `extends` first — fixed in the same session, 8 truth rows added, unexplained 2 -> 0 at a 400-file sample — and then `overrides`. Without it `overrides` is invisible: its edges sit at 0.5, so the harness files them as `heuristic`, and a bucket full of suspicion reads as caution rather than as a hole. That is why X9 could be closed honestly as 'true edges the truth cannot adjudicate' and why that closure was still incomplete: the bucket also held edges that are simply wrong. **THE FULL-CORPUS POPULATION, 3,369 files: 50 override edges naming a qualified base, across 7 builtin bases.** They are not equivalent rows. TRUE members (the base really has them): `URLSearchParams.*` — append, delete, entries, forEach, get, getAll, has, keys, set, sort, toString, values, [Symbol.iterator]; `Map.*` — clear, delete, entries, forEach, get, has, keys, set, values, [Symbol.iterator]; `Set.*` — add, clear, delete, entries, forEach, has, keys, values. **CANNOT BE MEMBERS — the defects.** (a) PRIVATE AND IMPLEMENTATION NAMES, 8 of 50: `URLSearchParams.#update_url`, `URLSearchParams.[REPLACE]`, `Map.#read_all`, `Map.#source`, `Set.#init`, `Set.#source`, `Date.#init`, `HTMLElement.$$g_p`. A `#name` is a private field, scoped to the class body and NOT a prototype member, so it cannot override anything on a base; `[REPLACE]` is a template marker and `$$g_p` is a Svelte-internal field. (b) CUSTOM-ELEMENT CALLBACKS, 3 of 50: `HTMLElement.connectedCallback`, `.disconnectedCallback`, `.attributeChangedCallback` — hooks the browser INVOKES on a custom element, not members of HTMLElement, so nothing is overridden. (c) INHERITED, NOT OWN, 2 of 50: `HTMLElement.addEventListener` / `.removeEventListener` live on `EventTarget.prototype`. (d) NON-STANDARD, 2 of 50: `Error.toJSON`, `URL.toJSON`. So the analyzer's guess is right about 39 of 50 and wrong about 11. **THE MECHANISM IS NAMED BY THE ANALYZER ITSELF**: every one carries `reasonCode: "first-parent-guess"` and `evidenceClass: "inferred"` at confidence 0.5. The analyzer is not asserting these, it is guessing. **WHY 0.5 IS NOT SUFFICIENT, which is the judgement.** The tier does real work — it is why these are suspicion rather than fabrication. But X9's closure said the oracle cannot adjudicate them because no corpus contains `URL`; that was correct, and it is also why this is a defect rather than a boundary. An edge that cannot be adjudicated AND cannot be true is not a declared uncertainty, it is a wrong answer wearing one. The private-field and custom-element-callback rows are DECIDABLE — a `#name` is never a prototype member — so they are not in the heuristic bucket's intended population at all.
gaps.status: OPEN — the `overrides` oracle does not exist, and 11 of the 50 emitted edges are unfounded
gaps.closure: Two separable pieces. (1) Derive `overrides` truth for the DECIDABLE cases — a base declared in the same file, or resolvable within it — which adjudicates those rows and leaves the unresolvable ones as declared suspicion. (2) Decide the design question for unresolvable bases: either stop emitting, or narrow the rule so a `#private` field and a custom-element callback can never match. The blast radius is real (the reasonCode, the confidence model, and a fixture that pins current behaviour), so (2) is not decided by this finding. Until it is, those ~11 rows are real output and the label must not be counted as verified coverage.

decisions.question: AnalyzeContext.overrideCompanion is never populated by production callers — what must the analyzer do for externally-declared bases?
decisions.resolution: M37.10 ruling (family-wide): the companion is optional enrichment, never a hard gate. In-file base declaring the method -> verified override @0.95; companion present -> companion-index resolution; otherwise deterministic Pass-3 first-parent guess @0.5 with reasonCode 'first-parent-guess' and tier 'inferred' — below the patterns.ts 0.7 threshold, counted as heuristic by the F5 differential. Gating on the companion alone silently dropped every cross-file override. Gated by F9-PROBE-M3710-JAVASCRIPT, the javascript/external-override fixture + confidence pins, and 6 family regression mutants.

decisions.question: Does the javascript lane's truth carry calls?
decisions.ruling: YES after #611: deriveJavaScriptEdges is pushed into the sweep truth for the plain javascript lane (the analyzer-side filter already compared calls; without the push, truth emitted ZERO calls and every analyzer call surfaced unexplained — 294 in the first gated vue-core run; per-file parity on scripts/verify-commit.js was proven during the wave).

decisions.question: Review J1: bySource keyed qualified_calls by bare method name, so U.save + O.save shared one union payload. How to key without breaking object-literal members (ownerKind Constant)?
decisions.decision: Owner-qualified keys (Owner::method) for class-owned methods; bare keys everywhere else, mirrored on the symbol-attachment side by the same rule (ownerKind Class qualifies). Prototype assignments resolve Owner::method through the existing prototype branch. Fixture javascript/duplicate-method pins per-owner includes/notIncludes both directions; mutant javascript/dup-first-wins also covers the J3 half.

decisions.question: Review J2: owner-only matching paired methods against same-named FIELDS (0.95, empty metadata) and emitted constructor overrides; the guess tier fired even for in-file bases that provably lack the method.
decisions.decision: Pair only against base METHODS (kind-gated both sides); constructors never pair; verified pairs carry reasonCode verified-in-file; the 0.5 guess fires only for bases outside the file (in-file absence is proof of non-override, not an unknown). Fixture javascript/override-qualification (pair + three forbids); mutants javascript/override-field-pair + javascript/override-ctor.

decisions.question: Review J3: first-wins dedup kept the dead redeclaration while runtime and TS keep the last body.
decisions.decision: Last-wins replace via owner:name index (shared with prototype assignments, which genuinely overwrite at runtime); superseded body spans recorded so nested symbols prune and relationship passes skip dead subtrees (module helper isNodeInDeadSpans). Fixture javascript/duplicate-method (qualified_calls + dead-call forbid); covered by the dup-first-wins mutant.

The claim probe now asserts the pinned behavior so a drive-by 'fix' fails loudly.

decisions.question: M49 #758 B5: get/set pairs collapsed to ONE symbol via the owner:name J3 dedup key — the getter was deadSpanned (nested symbols pruned, body calls skipped) and the setter's body walked under the getter's slot. Also: what happens when a DATA member shares the name (get x + x())?
decisions.decision: RULED - FIXED: accessor pairs are DISTINCT descriptor slots (Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor returns {get, set}) — both Property symbols survive with metadata.accessorKind, and BOTH bodies walk (calls/uses/symbols). Runtime slot semantics kept honest: a DATA member REPLACES the whole descriptor slot (get x then x() kills the accessor entirely — both halves removed, bodies deadSpanned); an accessor takes over a data member's slot; get+set MERGE (coexist). Cross-kind kills are post-walk zombies (mid-walk splice would corrupt seenMethodIdx indices). Pinned by javascript/accessor-slot-semantics + 3 mutants (accessor-pair-collapse, data-slot-zombie, static-override-fabrication).

decisions.question: M49 #758 B4: Sub { static greet() {} } fabricated overrides Base.greet at 0.95 — static and instance members live in DIFFERENT namespaces (no prototype-chain link between Sub.greet and Base.prototype.greet).
decisions.decision: RULED - FIXED: extractOverrideRelationships skips isStatic symbols (continue before base lookup). Control proves non-vacuous: instance greet both sides still emits Sub.greet->Base.greet. Oracle parity: deriveTreeEdges never derived JS overrides truth (in-file branch has no js method_definition registration) — the lane audits analyzer overrides against empty truth, so the B4 fix REDUCES unexplained fabrications with zero oracle change. Mutant static-override-fabrication re-adds the edge; forbidRelationships kills it.

decisions.node_type: export { x as default } alias-default clause
decisions.question: M49 #758 B8: name "default" with isDefault:false lost the public binding name while export default y worked. Fix or verify co-agent's landed fix?
decisions.decision: RULED - VERIFIED ALREADY-FIXED (independent probe, this wave): the analyzer emits {name:"default", isDefault:true, metadata:{viaAliasDefault:true, localName:"x"}} — J6's alias contract (public name recorded) plus the default flag. Probe conv-j-b8.ts re-run at HEAD confirms. No new fixture needed: the B8 shape is pinned by the export-uniqueness family gate; the accessor-slot fixture's export surface is unaffected.

decisions.node_type: binding positions (import bindings, parameters, catch params, destructuring/pattern targets, export specifiers)
decisions.question: M49 W1 (#768): the #744 bare-read walk listed only declaration NAMES as definition sites, so every other binding position fabricated `uses @0.6` edges. Is a binding site a read?
decisions.decision: RULED - NO. A binding position is a DEFINITION and emits no read edge. Fix landed on the analyzer (real-javascript-analyzer.ts) AND the JS lane oracle (deriveJavaScriptEdges) in the same commit; pinned by fixture javascript/binding-sites-are-not-reads (3 regression mutants: import-binding / param / destructure-target fabrication) and by F9-PROBE-JSD-BINDINGS, which additionally asserts the ORACLE does not derive the forbidden names. The RIGHT side of a pattern default (`value = seed`) stays a read.

decisions.node_type: oracle-vs-analyzer collusion (process, not a grammar shape)
decisions.question: M49 W1: the javascript lane reported 100/0/0 while both sides fabricated uses for binding positions. Oracle lockstep (the C5 standing lesson) mirrored a defect instead of catching it. What stops a lane from agreeing on a wrong contract?
decisions.decision: RULED - a lane cannot independently verify a surface whose truth is mirrored from the same contract. Two guards: (1) F9-PROBE-JSD-BINDINGS runs with oracleForbid enabled, so an oracle that derives a forbidden edge fails the battery as `oracle colludes` (new probeLang capability, reusable by every future probe; self-tested by re-introducing the fabrication and watching it fail); (2) every analyzer behavior change must be pinned by an F3 fixture asserting the SEMANTIC contract (forbidden edges), not only by lane counts.

decisions.node_type: member-chain assignment LHS (write) — subtree vs node suppression
decisions.question: M49 W1: `document.getElementById(id).style.display = v` lost the read of `id` and of `style`, and `store.inner.limit = v` lost `store`/`inner`. The suppression used `continue` in a stack walk that pushes children at the loop tail, so the whole STATEMENT SUBTREE was skipped. What does a write suppress?
decisions.decision: RULED - the write LHS suppresses ONLY its own target node, never the subtree. Reads nested inside the statement (call arguments, intermediate chain segments, the RHS) must survive; the write target itself (`limit`, `display`) must not emit a read. Implemented as a per-node guard (`if (!isWrite)`) so the tail child-push still runs. Pinned by fixture javascript/write-lhs-nested-reads with two mutants (write-lhs-subtree-skip, write-target-read-leak). Found only because the #760 cold-pool rotation sampled never-sampled files (grails-core MISSING=7, lodash MISSING=26) - no fixture had ever covered the shape, and the code comment asserted the opposite of what it did.

decisions.question: M49 W1: for a call-rooted chain the head was emitted as raw node TEXT, so `document.getElementById(id).style = v` produced `uses -> document.getElementById(id)` — a target that is not a symbol. Emit or not?
decisions.decision: RULED - the chain head is a read only when it IS an identifier (the chain-root contract). A call/literal head carries no symbol; the call already has its `calls` edge. Analyzer + oracle gated identically; pinned by javascript/write-lhs-nested-reads (`targetEndsWith` forbid) and mutant javascript/chain-head-expression-fabrication.

decisions.node_type: member identity inside object literals (dedup scope)
decisions.question: M49 W2 (#769): the method dedup key was `${owner ?? "module"}:${name}` and scopeOwnerName only reports CLASS scopes, so every object-literal member of a module shared ONE slot. Two init()s in sibling objects, or two Vue prop-default() factories, collapsed: the later replaced the earlier, dead-spanning its body and dropping its calls. Is a member's identity its bare name in the module?
decisions.decision: RULED - NO. Identity is CONTAINER-SCOPED: class body -> class name (unchanged), object literal -> the literal's span (obj@<startIndex>). Sibling containers never collide; duplicates INSIDE one container still collapse last-wins (J3 + the dup-key Option A ruling) because they share the key. Also fixed the B5 sibling-accessor kill, which matched owner+name TEXT and so also killed same-named accessors of OTHER object literals - it now resolves the exact sibling slot key. Analyzer-only (the JS lane truth oracle derives both calls site-agnostically, so lockstep was already correct here); pinned by javascript/sibling-object-member-identity (init count=2 + calls init->one) and mutants javascript/sibling-object-collapse, vue/prop-default-multi-collapse.

decisions.node_type: fixture authoring from a corpus file (process, not a grammar shape)
decisions.question: M49 W2: #762 closed as `verified ALREADY-FIXED` on vue/prop-default-factory-calls - a fixture with ONE factory, whose assertions pass with or without the sibling-object collision - while the corpus file (MarkdownEditor) kept MISSING={toFixed,random}. What must a corpus-derived fixture reproduce?
decisions.decision: RULED - the corpus file's ACTUAL shape, including the interaction that makes it fail. A one-factory reconstruction of a two-factory file tested an adjacent shape and produced false confidence for two waves. Re-authored vue/prop-default-factory-calls to the real shape (two sibling factories + interleaved plain `default:` members) and verified it FAILS against the pre-fix code (mutant vue/prop-default-multi-collapse) before accepting the green.

decisions.question: M49 W4 rotated-sample finding (ledger J6): the template-substitution walk emitted Uses for EVERY identifier in the substitution subtree, so ${fn(x)} fabricated `uses fn` and ${obj.m(x)} fabricated `uses obj` - 5 corpus edges (benchmarking/utils.js, transform-template/template.js) that the F5 truth rightly refused; the walk's own sibling rule nine lines up excludes callees (!isCallee).
decisions.decision: RULED - a substituted identifier is a read only when it is not part of a call's callee expression and not an assignment target; the walk gates on ancestor containment (call `function` span / assignment `left` span) and, per the TS TSD28 family contract, owns the substitution read alone (the general bare-read rule's duplicate is suppressed: one interpolated read = ONE Uses edge at 0.85 isTemplateInterpolation). Analyzer-only fix; the oracle already excluded callees, so parity was restored, not negotiated.
decisions.evidence: fixture javascript/template-substitution-reads (forbid uses fn/obj + count==1); mutants javascript/template-callee-uses + javascript/template-read-duplicate CAUGHT; F3 javascript 55/55; F4 full battery 449/449 (0 survivors); corpus re-probe at the fixed tree: svelte-repo javascript lane 0 unexplained (was 5)

decisions.question: M49 W13 (deep-measurement finding; W12 residual): only class_declaration pushed a Class scope, so scopeOwnerName returned undefined for every member of every ANONYMOUS class expression and they ALL shared the dedup key `module:<name>` - the second class expression's `constructor` (and any same-named method) replaced the first, dead-spanning its body and dropping every edge it owned. Measured on the svelte corpus: custom-element.js defines TWO class expressions (the SvelteElement custom-element base, and the per-component Class inside create_custom_element), each with a constructor, so this.attachShadow(shadow_root_init) in the FIRST vanished - the second javascript-lane MISSING edge W12's 400-file measurement registered. The 60-file rotation never sampled a file with two anonymous class expressions, which is why the deep run found it and no fixture did.
decisions.decision: RULED - a member's identity is container-scoped (W2 #769 for object literals, now class bodies too): when no declared class name exists, the containing class_body's span is the container key. Duplicates INSIDE one class still collapse last-wins (J3 / dup-key Option A). Pinned by fixture javascript/class-expression-member-identity (constructor count=2, run count=2, calls constructor->attachShadow and calls run->alpha - both LOST pre-fix) with mutant javascript/class-expression-container-collapse.

decisions.question: M49 W13 (deep-measurement finding; W12 residual): the member-segment dedup key was `${source}.${seg}`, and a private segment's text is literally `#x` - so the key became `${source}.#` + `x`, BYTE-IDENTICAL to the bare-read/chain-root key of the plain identifier `x` (`${source}.#` + `x`). Whichever node was walked first claimed it. Measured on the svelte corpus: packages/svelte/src/reactivity/set.js - the field initializer `#update_version = update_version || -1` (line 52) reads the IMPORTED binding update_version first, claiming key SvelteSet.#update_version, so the genuine read this.#update_version (line 88) was dropped as a duplicate - the FIRST javascript-lane MISSING edge W12's 400-file measurement registered. #version/#size survived only because no plain binding of those names is read in the same container.
decisions.decision: RULED - a private segment's key uses a `#`-marked namespace (`${source}.$private${seg}`); `#` cannot appear inside an identifier, so no bare/root/segment key can collide with it and the private read and the same-named bare read are distinct edges that never suppress each other. The emitted target keeps the `#` spelling. Pinned by fixture javascript/private-member-read-identity (uses Store->#update_version LOST pre-fix) with mutant javascript/private-read-key-collision.

decisions.question: F8 re-audit (M60 javascript deep review): `class` sat in handled_verified.types while the analyzer emits NO Class symbol for a class EXPRESSION - the overclaim the lane formula forbids ('green with committed evidence OR explicitly ruled'). Is the absence a gap, a defect, or a deliberate design decision?
decisions.decision: RULED - the class EXPRESSION deliberately emits no Class symbol; it is not a gap. A class expression is a VALUE expression, so the binding that holds it is its identity - the same reason a function expression yields no Function symbol and is pinned by javascript/class-expression-unresolved. Probed all four binding forms at f10ea18f: `class S{}` -> S:class (class_declaration, the Class symbol case, still handled); `const C = class{}` -> C:constant + m:method; `const C = class Inner{}` -> C:constant + m:method; `let C; C = class{}` -> C:variable + m:method; `sink(class{})` -> no symbol at all. Critically, heritage is NOT lost - it is re-anchored onto the binding: `class S extends Base` -> extends:S->Base + uses:S->Base, while `const C = class extends Base` -> extends:C->Base + uses:T->Base (JD4). An unbound anonymous class emits nothing (extends:C->Base is refused rather than fabricated), which is the lane's standing rule: an unresolved edge is honest, a wrong one is not. The method m:method survives in every form with its container taken from the class_body span - JSD30. So: the DECLARATION path is handled and fixture-pinned; the EXPRESSION path is a deliberate attribution choice, pinned by javascript/class-expression-heritage and javascript/class-expression-member-identity.

decisions.question: F8 re-audit: the census injects ERROR and MISSING into every language's node-type set (completeness-inventory.ts:609 — they are not in the wasm symbol table, so the gate adds them by hand), yet no javascript spec row claimed them, so section-a failed for javascript and for 10+ other lanes on the same pair. Gap, silent omission, or handled?
decisions.decision: RULED - HANDLED, and this is the javascript analog of bash BD5 (which the gate's own comment at completeness-inventory.ts:601-608 cites as the precedent: 'a spec that classifies ERROR - correctly, since the analyzer consults it - was being told its own row was grammar drift ... the fix is never to delete the correct row'). javascript holds an EXPLICIT guard, real-javascript-analyzer.ts:302: `if (n.type === "ERROR" || n.isMissing)`, which records a warning on result.errors and skips the damaged subtree. ERROR is therefore handled_verified: the analyzer consults it on purpose, exactly as bash does at real-bash-analyzer.ts:663/703/715. The guard is SCOPED to the damaged region, never a blanket file refusal - the property BD5 insists on, because a blanket refusal swallows valid declarations in a partially broken file. Measured at f10ea18f: `function good(){} function bad( { } const x = ;` -> good:function SURVIVES; the same file with the damage first -> BOTH x:constant and good:function survive; `function good(){} const arr = [1, 2` (unterminated) -> good:function survives, the array yielding only uses:T->arr. A clean control emits the same good:function with no errors, and a wholly-damaged file yields symbols:[] with one warning per ERROR. MISSING is filed internal_silent: the same guard reports it, but it contributes no symbol of its own. No fabrication is possible here - an unresolved name stays unresolved.
